style: mother writing in her second language: simple sentences, slightly off grammar and tense, American words

situations.name: Getting a flu shot at the pediatrician
situations.feared_outcome: The needle will break off inside my arm

behaviors.text: Refuses to get out of the car in the clinic parking lot
Asks again and again whether there will be a shot today
Ran out of the exam room when the nurse came in with the tray

accommodations.text: Mom canceled and rescheduled the flu shot appointment
Mom promised 'no shot today' to get him into the building

situations.name: Dentist cleaning (the trigger is gagging on the tools, not needles)
situations.feared_outcome: I will throw up in front of the dentist

behaviors.text: Keeps his hand half raised the whole cleaning, ready to signal stop
Asks for a break every minute or so to sit up and swallow

accommodations.text: Mom asked the dentist to skip the x-rays

situations.name: Health class video showing a blood draw

behaviors.text: Left class for the bathroom partway through the video and stayed out until it ended

accommodations.text: Mom emailed the teacher asking that he be excused from videos like that

monitoring_log.child_behavior_observed: He is not want to get out from the car. He lock the door and cry. We sit in parking lot 25 minutes.
monitoring_log.parent_response: I call the office and cancel. We make new appointment for October.

monitoring_log.child_behavior_observed: He go in the chair ok. But all the time his hand is up a little, like he is ready to say stop. He ask for break many times, he sit up and swallow.
monitoring_log.parent_response: I tell the dentist please no x-ray this time, last time he almost vomit with the x-ray thing.

monitoring_log.situation: Talking at dinner about the doctor
monitoring_log.child_behavior_observed: He ask me is there shot next time, is there shot, maybe 10 times in the dinner.
monitoring_log.parent_response: I say I don't know yet. Then I say ok no shot, to make him stop.

monitoring_log.child_behavior_observed: Teacher show video of nurse take blood from arm. He go to bathroom and not come back until video is finish. Teacher tell me after.
monitoring_log.parent_response: I write email to teacher, please he don't need to watch this kind of video.

monitoring_log.child_behavior_observed: He come inside the building because I promise him no shot today. In the room the nurse come with the tray and he run out to the hallway and to the waiting room.
monitoring_log.parent_response: I go after him. Nurse say we can do another day. I feel bad because I lie to him about no shot.

monitoring_log.parent_words: In the car he tell me finally why he is so scared. He think the needle will break and stay inside his arm. His friend tell him this happen to somebody. I say this is not true but he don't believe me.

monitoring_log.child_behavior_observed: He ask again if he have to get shot this week. Ask 3 or 4 times.
monitoring_log.parent_response: I say we talk with the doctor lady first.

voice_notes.text: ok so today um the dentist they call for remind the next cleaning and he hear me on the phone and he say mom tell them no x-ray tell them and um he was ok after but he ask me two times if it is the same dentist
voice_notes.trap: dentist call is about gagging and x-rays, not needles; 'two times' is a count, not a fear level

voice_notes.text: this morning he ask me again about the shot is there shot is there shot and I say I don't know and he say it is a nine for him the shot like a nine um and then in the afternoon we drive past the clinic and he don't want to look at the building
voice_notes.trap: second moment (not looking at the building) is not a listed behavior; do not invent one with a type

turns.text: Good afternoon, Arjun. Good afternoon, Mrs. Rao. Come sit. Thank you for writing in the log every day this week, Mrs. Rao. It helps a lot. I'd like to go over it together. Arjun, is it okay if we talk about the doctor and the dentist today?
I guess. As long as there's no shot here.
There are no shots in this office. I don't have any needles at all. We just talk and plan. Okay. Mrs. Rao, the first entry was the flu shot in September. You sat in the parking lot.

Yes. He lock the door from inside. Twenty-five minutes. He was crying, I was almost crying. In the end I call and cancel. Then we go on the new day, the third of October, and I tell him there is no shot, only checkup. I know this is not good. He come inside. But then the nurse come with the tray and he run. Out of the room, down the hallway, to the waiting room.
Thank you for being so honest about the promise. A lot of parents do that, and I understand why. Arjun, can you tell me what happened when the nurse came in?
She had the little tray with the stuff on it. And I saw the orange cap. And I just went. I didn't even decide, my legs just went.
Your legs just went. That's a good way to describe it. That is your body's alarm going off. And your mom said you told her something in the car, about what you think could happen with the needle.
It could break. Like, the tip snaps off and it stays inside you. In your arm. And it goes around inside you.
Where did you hear about that?
Dev said his uncle's friend had it. Or his uncle. I don't remember.

Okay. That is a really scary picture to carry around. I'm not going to argue with you about it right now, because arguing doesn't usually make the scary picture go away. What I want to do instead is help your brain collect some real experience. On the thermometer, zero to ten, getting a flu shot. What number is that?
Nine. Not ten, because ten is like, a shark. But nine.
Nine, and a shark is ten. I like that you have a ten that's a shark. Now, I noticed in the log, Mrs. Rao, that he asks you a lot, is there a shot, is there a shot.
Every day. At dinner ten times. At bedtime. I say I don't know, then he ask again, then I say okay no shot, to stop it.

I'd like to talk about that, because I think it's keeping the fear going. When he asks and he gets an answer, he feels better for a little while. Then the worry comes back. So he asks again. And when the answer is 'no shot' and then there is a shot, he learns he can't trust the answer, so he asks even more. I want to try a different way. You tell him the truth one time, and after that you say, 'You already know the answer, and I know this is hard.' And then you talk about something else.
Okay. It will be hard for me. But okay.
It is hard. Now, the dentist. I want to check something with you, Arjun, because I think the dentist might be a different worry. Is the dentist scary because of needles too?
No. They don't do shots at cleanings. It's the thing they put in your mouth for the picture. The x-ray thing. And the water sucker. It makes me want to throw up.
So at the dentist, the scary part is gagging, maybe throwing up in front of the dentist. Not needles.
Yeah. If I throw up on her that would be so embarrassing.
I thought it is the same thing. Doctor and dentist, both. I am surprised.

That's really useful to know, and it's an easy mix-up. They look alike from the outside, both are appointments in a chair with someone in a white coat, but the fear inside is different. So we'll treat them as two separate things. What number is the dentist, Arjun?
Like a five. It's not that bad. I just keep my hand up so I can stop her.
Five. Okay. We'll leave the dentist for later, since the next cleaning isn't for a while. Mrs. Rao, there was also the health class video?
Yes, one time. The teacher show a video of blood test. He go to bathroom until it finish. I write to the teacher to say he don't have to watch.

Okay, I'm going to write that down and we'll come back to it. I would ask you not to send any more emails like that for now, until we talk about it more. Let's focus on the shot. Here's what I'm thinking. We are not going to the doctor this week. We're going to build up slowly. Arjun, at home, step one is looking at pictures of needles. Real ones, on the computer, with Mom. You look until the number goes down a bit.
Pictures are okay. Like a three.

Three. Then step two, I'm going to give your mom some alcohol wipes, the kind they use before a shot. You wipe a spot on your arm, and you hold a cap from a pen right there, against the skin, for ten seconds. No needle at all. What number is that?
Hmm. Five? Because it's like pretending.

Five is a good number to practice at. So pictures most days, and the wipe and pen cap three times this week. Mrs. Rao, you write down what number he says each time. And with the questions, you answer once, truthfully, and then you change the subject. Also, you don't promise 'no shot.' Is that a plan?
Yes. The pictures, the wipe with the pen, three times. And I don't say no shot. I answer one time only.
When do I have to get the real shot though?
Not this week. We'll decide that together, when you're ready, and your mom will tell you the truth about when it is. Deal?
Deal.
Great work today, Arjun. You told me a lot of hard stuff. I'll see you next week.

Arjun fainted or has a medical condition
